A vertical 9:16 black-and-white photograph that looks like a frame from a British charity television appeal. A well-fed man in his mid-fifties, an invented government chancellor with an ordinary, slightly jowly face, thinning sandy-grey hair and a soft double chin, sits alone at the far end of a very long polished oak dining table in a large Georgian country-house kitchen. He wears a camel cashmere overcoat over a pale blue Oxford shirt and rests both hands around a single bone-china teacup. He is small in the frame, centred, framed straight on from the near end of the table at seated eye level with a normal lens, and he gazes just off the lens with a sad, faraway look. Behind him are a cream Aga range, copper pans on hooks and a tall sash window with soft overcast daylight coming in from the left, falling off into grey shadow on the right. The rest of the table is bare. Shot on black-and-white film with visible grain, lifted greys, low contrast and a slight softness, as if caught mid slow push-in. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 black-and-white photograph styled like a slow-motion shot from a charity television appeal, seen from outside in the rain. A plump man in his fifties, an invented politician with a round, unremarkable face, heavy eyebrows and slightly flushed cheeks, stands inside a heated Victorian-style conservatory and looks out through the glass. He wears a navy quilted gilet over a lambswool jumper, and one hand is pressed flat against the pane. Rain runs down the glass in thick streaks and beads, partly blurring his face and the potted lemon tree and wicker armchair behind him. The camera is handheld at chest height, slightly off-centre, a little close to the glass, with the white-painted glazing bar cutting down one side of the frame. Flat grey daylight, soft and directionless, mid-grey tones throughout, lifted blacks, coarse film grain, a faint motion smear on the falling raindrops. His expression is quietly forlorn, eyes lowered. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 black-and-white close-up photograph from a British charity television appeal. The face of an invented man in his mid-fifties fills the upper two thirds of the frame: well fed, broad cheeks, a small neat grey beard, open pores, faint broken veins on the nose, deep crow's feet and slightly watery eyes looking straight down the lens with mournful sincerity. The collar of a charcoal herringbone tweed coat and a silk paisley scarf are visible at the bottom edge. Soft window light comes from the left, falling off into gentle shadow across the right cheek, with lifted greys and low contrast. The background is an out-of-focus wood-panelled study with a leather wing chair. Across the lower third sits a plain caption in clean white sans-serif lettering reading "This is Crispin." Shot on grainy black-and-white film with a slightly soft focus, framed with a little too much headroom. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph of the corner of a three-storey 1970s brick council block in an English town, taken from across the street at eye level on a tripod with a normal lens, so the walls stand straight and the building fills almost the whole frame, with only a thin band of flat grey sky above the roofline. It is the very end of dusk under a heavy overcast sky: no sun, no shadows, the light so low and even that the maroon-brown stretcher-bond brick and the slate-grey sky sit almost at the same dull brightness. Concrete bands run along each floor. The windows are fat white uPVC casements with top-hung openers, and their frames pick up a faint violet-blue edge from the sky. Every window is dark except two on the first floor, either side of the corner: the left one glows a flat orange-amber through a drawn curtain with no detail visible, the right one shows cream vertical blinds with a single bare ceiling bulb burning behind them. The picture is soft and slightly smeared, as if shot through fine drizzle on a long exposure, with lifted blacks, low contrast and almost no colour except the warmth in those two windows. Quiet, still, nobody in the street. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 colour photograph looking into the small front room of an elderly woman's council flat at dusk, taken from the hallway at eye level so the painted edge of the door frame cuts down the left side of the picture. Across the room, slightly off-centre, a woman in her early eighties sits in a worn armchair wearing a buttoned dark wool winter coat and a knitted bobble hat indoors, a crocheted blanket over her knees, both hands round a mug. She is small in the frame, watching an old boxy television on a low cabinet that throws a flickering grey-white light across her face; the screen shows a black and white picture. Behind her a window with white uPVC frames and net curtains is filled with cold blue-grey dusk. The walls are magnolia woodchip, there is an unlit wall-mounted gas fire with a wood-effect surround, a patterned carpet worn thin near the door, a carriage clock and framed family photos on the mantel, a draught excluder along the bottom of the door, a folded newspaper on the arm of the chair. No lamp is on: the only light is the window's cold blue and the TV's weak glow, low contrast, lifted shadows, soft focus at the edges, shot on grainy colour negative film. Lived-in and slightly untidy, nothing posed. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph taken from outside a ground-floor flat at dusk, standing on the pavement close to a single white uPVC window set in dark red-brown brick, the window filling most of the frame with a strip of rough brick and a concrete sill around it. Through slightly dirty, rain-speckled glass and half-open cream vertical blinds, a woman in her late seventies is seen side-on in a dark buttoned coat and a knitted hat, sitting very still in an armchair, lit only by the cold flickering grey light of a television just out of view inside the room; a bare ceiling bulb is switched off above her. Her face is lined, her grey hair uneven where it comes out under the hat. The outside light is a deep, even, slate-blue overcast twilight that tints the white window frame violet at its edges, and the brick is almost colourless. The image is soft and a little smeared, as from a phone night shot with heavy noise reduction, low contrast, lifted blacks, the only warmth a faint orange from a streetlamp reflected in one corner of the glass. Quiet and watched from outside. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph taken from low down on the floor of a narrow council-flat hallway at dusk, looking along a worn swirl-patterned carpet towards the inside of a white uPVC front door. The brass letterbox flap is still tilted open, and a small pile of junk mail has just landed on a thin brown coir doormat: a pizza menu, a window-cleaning leaflet, a brown envelope, and a glossy flyer face up whose bold white sans-serif headline reads "SPONSOR A CHANCELLOR" above a photo of a well-fed man in his fifties in an expensive camel coat looking mournfully into the lens. The only light is a cold grey-blue dusk coming through the frosted glass panel in the door, with a faint warm amber spill from a living-room doorway off to the left edge of frame. A draught excluder lies along the bottom of the door and a pair of old slippers sits off-centre near the skirting board. Low contrast, lifted blacks, soft and slightly smeared, shot on a consumer phone at night with visible noise and no crisp detail. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph looking straight down at a worn doormat just inside a council flat's front door, framed slightly off-centre so the bottom edge of the white door and a strip of patterned carpet cut into the top of the frame. Scattered across the mat lie a gas bill in a window envelope, a supermarket offers leaflet, a takeaway menu, and a postcard-sized flyer half covered by the menu, with the words "SPONSOR A CHANCELLOR" printed in bold white capitals on a black band and a black-and-white photo of a plump, comfortable middle-aged man in a tailored coat with a trembling, wounded expression. The toe of an old woman's fleece-lined slipper and the hem of her buttoned brown winter coat enter from the bottom edge. Flat, cold blue-grey light from a frosted door pane, very even and shadowless, with one weak warm glow on the carpet from a lamp out of frame. Shot on slightly grainy 1980s colour negative film, muted colours, low contrast. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 close-up photograph of an elderly woman's hand holding a glossy junk-mail flyer at chest height in a dim council-flat hallway, the cuff of her thick buttoned winter coat and the edge of a knitted glove pulled back at the wrist. Her hand is real and old: thin papery skin, liver spots, raised veins, a worn gold wedding ring, short unpainted nails. The flyer reads "SPONSOR A CHANCELLOR" in bold white sans-serif capitals, and under it is a photo of an invented well-fed man in his fifties in a navy cashmere coat, his face even sadder than a charity advert, eyes wet, lower lip unsteady, standing beside a gleaming car. Behind her hand, out of focus, a white uPVC door with a frosted glass panel lets in cold grey-blue dusk, and a warm amber light from another room catches one side of her knuckles. Normal lens, slightly off-centre, soft focus at the edges, low contrast and lifted blacks, like a noisy phone photo taken at night. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 close-up photograph of a British woman in her early eighties standing just inside her front door at dusk, looking down at a glossy A5 flyer held in both hands, its back to the camera so only her face and the top edge of the paper fill the frame. She wears a buttoned navy wool winter coat and a grey knitted bobble hat indoors, a pair of reading glasses low on her nose. Her face is soft with pity, brows slightly raised, mouth just parting as if about to speak, not a pout, not a smile. Her skin is thin and lined, with liver spots on her cheek and a few loose strands of uneven white hair escaping the hat. The only light is a cold, flat grey-blue from the frosted glass panel of the door on the left, with a faint warm orange spill from a hallway bulb behind her on the right; blacks are lifted and contrast is low. The camera is at her chest height looking slightly up, framed off-centre so her face sits in the upper third and the hat is cut by the top edge. Shot on a cheap consumer digital camera in low light, soft, slightly smeared, with visible noise and no crisp detail. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph of a narrow council-flat hallway at dusk, seen at eye level from the doorway of the front room, the painted door frame cutting into the left side of the picture. An elderly working-class British woman, about eighty, in a long brown winter coat, a burgundy knitted hat and fleece slippers, stands on a worn patterned doormat by the front door. A small pile of junk mail lies at her feet. She holds one flyer out at arm's length to read it, its face towards the camera: a sad, well-fed middle-aged man in an expensive coat above the words "SPONSOR A CHANCELLOR" in bold white sans-serif on red. She tilts her head with a look of genuine sympathy. The walls are magnolia woodchip, a draught excluder lies along the bottom of the door, and a coat hook is crowded with scarves and a shopping bag. The light is a single weak bare bulb overhead, warm and dim, against cold blue dusk through the reeded glass of the front door. Colour negative film with fine grain, low contrast, a normal lens, slightly high camera, nothing tidy. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 photograph taken from across the street at late blue hour, looking at the lower corner of a three-storey brown-brick council block under a flat overcast sky. The light is very low and even, with no shadows, the brick a cold slate grey shading to maroon, the blacks lifted and soft as if through drizzle. Only one ground-floor window is lit: behind a white uPVC frame with a violet-blue edge from the sky, cream vertical blinds are half open and a bare ceiling bulb glows warm amber. Through the gap, small in the frame, an elderly woman in a winter coat and knitted hat sits forward in an armchair, holding a sheet of paper close to her face and looking at it, the cold blue flicker of an old television on the far wall. The upper windows are dark. The camera is on a tripod at eye level, a normal-to-slightly-long lens, verticals straight, the building filling most of the frame with a sliver of grey sky at the top and the lit window placed low and off-centre. A long exposure with soft, smudged detail, quiet and lonely, in the manner of Todd Hido's night houses. Thanks.
